headline: Force field polarizability and sterol binding shape ion channel modeling
label: Ion Channel Computational Modeling
summary: Recent studies test how polarizable force fields, cholesterol-binding maps, and contact-energy statistics refine computational models of ion channels.
synthesis: The common thread is computational modeling of ion channels, with KcsA serving as a test system in two of the three items. The KcsA preprint compares nonpolarizable CHARMM36m, polarizable CHARMM-Drude, and ECC force fields for simulating 2D IR spectra, with the Drude model reported to better match the spectra, which underscores the role of electronic polarizability in spectroscopic simulation. A second study maps cholesterol-binding regions on TRPV6 across open and closed states using CG-MD, SILCS, and docking, and compares them with cryo-EM sterol densities. A third proposes a statistical method that groups residue-residue contact energies across aligned ion channel structures to identify folding determinants, tested on KcsA. What is new across these items is the emphasis on force-field choice, state-dependent lipid interactions, and data-driven energetic analysis of channel structures, rather than a single shared method.
